facts.fact: Kenya's AI and Emerging Technologies Policy had completed drafting and stakeholder consultation and was at legal review in the Attorney General's office, with a launch planned before the end of June 2026, KICTANet reports.
Dr. George Musumba, who chairs the policy's technical committee, says local language model development has early work visible in Swahili and Kikuyu.

facts.fact: Barrack Otieno of KICTANet says over 6,000 government services now operate exclusively through the eCitizen platform.

facts.fact: Gbenga Sesan of Paradigm Initiative says Kenya no longer scores well on internet shutdowns in the Londa 2025 report because there was a shutdown, including of Telegram.

KEN.note: KICTANet coordinated the drafting, but the document does not describe it as a research institution.

facts.fact: The Ministry of ICT's AI and Emerging Technologies Policy drafting, coordinated by KICTANet, included an inception workshop in November 2024, roundtables with civil society, academia, private sector and youth groups, sector webinars, a children's session and a public participation portal, and the consultation phase was complete by the session.
